item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate A directly and cleanly implements the frozen contract; Candidate B violates several explicit API, routing, and scope requirements.","reasons":["A adds the exact required Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption) signature.","A reuses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", then delegates to FilesService.Add, preserving existing option handling and error semantics.","A validates empty filenames and nil readers before requests and propagates multipart/source-reader errors.","A’s tests specifically cover multipart field, filename, content, retrying a non-seekable streamed reader, validation without requests, and source-reader failure propagation through Upload itself—not merely through the helper in isolation or indirectly through mandatory hidden gates. This is exactly the contract’s verification surface and materially stronger than B’s Upload tests, which omit an explicit source-reader-error case and use strings.NewReader in the retry test rather than demonstrating streamed/non-seekable input. Both candidates passed hidden behavior, but A’s visible tests better protect the reported regression and future maintenance. A is also much easier to review because its implementation is focused and relies on established machinery instead of duplicating it inside Upload. Its only visible testing gap is that Upload does not separately assert FilesOption forwarding, although delegation to Add makes that behavior direct and existing Add coverage should continue to apply. B tests more ancillary behavior, but much of that test volume covers out-of-contract association options and retry refactoring rather than the required API contract, so it does not outweigh A’s more targeted coverage. A’s validation uses direct fmt.Errorf strings rather than shared sentinel or wrapped validation errors, but the frozen contract does not prescribe error identity, and B uses the same strings for the two required input checks. B’s docs are more extensive, but they document behavior introduced by contract-violating changes and therefore are not a merge-quality advantage for this task."],"risks_a":["No dedicated test explicitly verifies that FilesOption values are forwarded by Upload, though delegation to Add makes the path straightforward.","The new validation errors are plain strings rather than typed or sentinel errors; the contract does not require error identity."],"risks_b":["Upload has opts ...FilesUploadOption instead of the exact required opts ...FilesOption signature, changing compatibility and option semantics.","Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates request construction, decoding, and error handling, contrary to the required single path.","It adds association fields and several WithFile...ID APIs despite the explicit instruction not to add association fields or change FilesOption behavior. This creates a second option hierarchy (FilesUploadOption / FilesRequestOption) and changes WithFilesRequestOptions’ return type, expanding public API surface and increasing maintenance and compatibility risk even if source calls still compile in common cases. Because Upload’s option type differs from Add’s, existing callers cannot uniformly pass arbitrary FilesOption values (for example WithFilesQuery), directly violating the requested convenience API contract. Its multipart helper expansion (Field and NewFileWithFields) is unnecessary for the task and makes the helper responsible for unrelated association semantics. The Upload implementation also reimplements Add’s Raw.Do invocation, Content-Type wiring, response envelope decoding, nil-data check, and request-option handling; future changes to Add could drift from Upload. The Raw.Do seekable-body retry refactor is explicitly out of scope and changes ownership/closing semantics globally. Beyond scope, that refactor’s GetBody closure rewinds and returns the same shared io.ReadSeeker for every replay rather than independent readers, which is fragile if GetBody is invoked more than once or concurrently and broadens subtle transport semantics. B’s Add retry test also does not set RetryAllMethods: true, so depending on default retry policy it may be testing behavior different from the user-reported POST configuration; mandatory gates passed, but the visible test is less explicit than A’s. The changelog and README advertise the out-of-contract association and global Raw.Do behavior, cementing APIs and semantics that should not be introduced in this patch."]}
